title: Multicalibration for Unbiased Model-Based Prevalence Estimation
abstract: arXiv:2604.21549v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Estimating the prevalence of a category in a population using imperfect measurement devices (diagnostic tests, classifiers, or large language models) is fundamental to science, public health, and online trust and safety. Standard approaches correct for known device error rates but assume these rates remain stable across populations. We show this assumption fails under covariate shift and that multicalibration, which enforces calibration conditional on the input features rather than just on average, is sufficient for unbiased prevalence estimation under such shift. Standard calibration and quantification methods fail to provide this guarantee. Our work connects recent theoretical work on fairness to a longstanding measurement problem spanning nearly all academic disciplines. A simulation confirms that standard methods exhibit bias growing with shift magnitude, while a multicalibrated estimator maintains near-zero bias. While we focus

translated_title: 用于无偏基于模型流行率估计的多重校准
translated_abstract: 使用不完善的测量设备（诊断测试、分类器或大语言模型）来估计人群中某一类别的流行率，对科学、公共卫生以及在线信任与安全至关重要。标准方法会对已知的设备错误率进行校正，但假设这些错误率在不同人群之间保持稳定。我们证明这一假设在协变量偏移下会失效，并表明多重校准——即在给定输入特征的条件下强制校准，而不仅仅是在平均意义上校准——足以在此类偏移下实现无偏的流行率估计。标准的校准与量化方法无法提供这一保证。我们的工作将近期关于公平性的理论研究成果与一个横跨几乎所有学科领域的长期测量问题联系起来。仿真实验证实，标准方法的偏差会随偏移幅度的增大而增长，而多重校准估计器则能保持接近于零的偏差。（摘要在此处被截断）
tldr: 本文证明了在协变量偏移条件下，多重校准（而非标准校准方法）足以保证基于模型的流行率估计无偏，从而将公平性领域的理论成果与横跨多学科的长期测量问题联系起来。
en_tdlr: This paper proves that multicalibration, rather than standard calibration, is sufficient for unbiased model-based prevalence estimation under covariate shift, connecting recent fairness theory to a longstanding measurement problem spanning nearly all academic disciplines.
